findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify when and how the digest-and-embed build executes relative to the synchronous read-path catch-up: bound per-create embedding work (or move the build off the create read path entirely), and state how a fresh or invalidated corpus converges to full current-key coverage so cosine ranking resumes without blocking a create.
evidence: Plan: 'it replaces only the scoring function and adds the digest-and-embed build step'
Plan: 'rebar cosine-ranks only when EVERY live entry carries a current-key vector, and otherwise degrades'

Sibling 47c8 implements catch-up SYNCHRONOUSLY in the read path: src/rebar/similar/__init__.py find_similar() calls catch_up() inline before search(), and similar_tickets_advisory (recent_creates.py:189-204) invokes find_similar on the post-write create path

Lexical re-indexing is local (one stat per dir, no transaction on the warm path per catchup.py); an embed+digest step is network-bound per ticket (one provider embed + one 40k-char digest LLM call), structurally unlike the work the read path is designed to absorb

ABSENCE: the plan names the build step and the current-key invalidation but never states where the build executes, whether per-create read-path work is bounded, or how a large invalidated corpus converges back to full coverage
findings.finding: The plan does not specify WHEN the digest-and-embed build runs relative to the synchronous read-path catch-up, so a fresh or invalidated corpus risks embedding/digesting every ticket synchronously on a user's create — thousands of network round-trips blocking the write path — and the all-or-nothing cosine gate stays degraded until that unbounded build completes, with no stated convergence story.
findings.location: Constraints -> 'Cosine ranking requires full current-key coverage'; 'Portability comes from the lexical tier' ('adds the digest-and-embed build step')
scenarios: embedding_model configured on an install whose index already holds thousands of live tickets; the next create triggers a full-corpus embed/digest
operator repins the digest-prompt commit or changes embedding_model, invalidating all entries; the next create must re-embed the whole corpus before cosine ranking resumes
a burst of new tickets leaves some entries without a current-key vector, so the gate degrades every create until the build catches up

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify `digest_failed`'s increment condition (a reply unparseable on both the first attempt and the single retry) and the terminal fallback for that path (degrade behaviour and whether the build proceeds), co-located with the empties/unparsed rules.
evidence: Plan: 'increments `digest_unparsed` and is retried once; a retry that succeeds counts as a success and leaves `digest_failed` at 0.'
`digest_failed` appears only ever as '... leaves `digest_failed` at 0' — its increment trigger is never stated
ADR 0122 says the two refusing tickets 'Both succeeded on retry', so the plan has no measured guidance for a retry that fails, yet must still define the outcome
No AC covers the retry-also-fails path; AC16/AC17 only cover first-attempt-unparse and retry-success
findings.finding: The digest counter `digest_failed` is referenced but its increment condition is never specified, and the fallback for a retry that also yields no recoverable mapping is undefined.
scenarios: A digest reply yields no recoverable mapping on the first attempt and ALSO on the single retry
An executor must decide whether to increment `digest_failed`, degrade that ticket, and whether the build continues
findings.suggested_fix: In the Digest step, add: a reply still yielding no object carrying the field names after the one retry increments `digest_failed` (and leaves that ticket unvectored, which triggers the whole-corpus degrade per the current-key coverage rule); add an AC asserting `digest_failed` is 1 on a reply that is unparseable twice.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per affected arm, the disposition surfaced on provider failure: say explicitly whether a transient/retryable provider failure (throttle/429) is surfaced as retryable (exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY) or is intentionally collapsed into the exit-0 lexical degrade, and justify that the always-local lexical fallback cannot itself mask a more-recoverable leg.
evidence: 'Degrade means retrieval returns the lexical tier's whole-corpus results, the create advisory carries them, a diagnostic is emitted and create exits 0.'
AC12: 'A provider denial or timeout degrades. Test: parameterize over both failures; assert exit status, advisory and diagnostic.'

rebar disposition vocabulary (exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY / classify_llm_failure): a 429 throttle is normally a retryable disposition, and the plan does not say whether it is surfaced as retryable or intentionally collapsed into exit-0 degrade.
findings.finding: The plan collapses every provider failure — 'a provider denial or timeout' (AC12) and partial-corpus coverage — uniformly into degrade-to-lexical + exit 0, without stating the disposition of a transient/retryable provider failure. A provider throttle/429 is normally retryable in rebar (exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY), but degrading it to an exit-0 lexical advisory masks that retryable condition behind a non-retryable disposition — the 1c0d shape.
findings.location: Constraints → 'Degrade' definition; AC12 'A provider denial or timeout degrades.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' note: embedding/digest provider failures (denial, timeout, ImportError, throttle) all degrade to the lexical advisory at exit 0 by design because surfacing must always happen; the retryable disposition is preserved by emitting it in the diagnostic (naming the failure class via classify_llm_failure) even though create still exits 0, so a transient throttle remains observable as retryable rather than silently indistinguishable from a permanent provider-absent degrade.

The plan names no existing module for the JSON/balanced-object/preamble-stripping portion; only YAML decode and single-wrapper-key unwrap are not already in structured.py
ANTI-FP FP7: structured.py is production code under src/rebar/llm/, not evals/ or a *_poc — rebuild-vs-extend is a genuine NIH question, not an intended reference-to-rebuild lifecycle
findings.finding: The digest reply-recovery pipeline (JSON-or-YAML decode, first-balanced-object extraction, prose-preamble stripping, wrapper-key unwrap, field-name screen) duplicates machinery already present in src/rebar/llm/structured.py, and the plan does not say whether it extends that module or reimplements it.

scenarios: A digest reply arrives as JSON behind a prose preamble — structured.py already recovers this today; a parallel implementation risks diverging behavior and a second maintenance surface
A reply wrapped in a ticket_digest key — _candidate_dicts' key-overlap screen already handles unwrapping-by-field-match, which the plan re-specifies as a bespoke single-wrapper-key unwrap
findings.suggested_fix: Build the digest recovery on structured.py's existing JSON/fenced/balanced-object + key-overlap machinery, adding only a YAML-decode fallback and the single-wrapper-key unwrap where they are genuinely new; reference the module in the Digest step so the shared path is explicit.
